title: Algebraization of a completion quotient with torsion conormal
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring, let $I\subset A$ be an ideal, let $B$ be a finite type $A$-algebra, and let $B^\wedge\twoheadrightarrow C$ be a surjective map from the $I$-adic completion of $B$ with kernel $J$. If $I^c(J/J^2)=0$ for some $c\ge0$, then $C$ is isomorphic as an $A$-algebra to the $I$-adic completion of a finite type $A$-algebra. Here $J/J^2$ denotes the quotient $B^\wedge$-module, and annihilation means multiplication by every element of the extended ideal $I^c$ is zero. [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]

proof.text: Put $S=B^\wedge$ and $K=IB$. The finite-type Noetherian permanence theorem makes $B$ Noetherian; its completion $S$ is Noetherian and $IS$-adically complete. In particular the ideals $J\subseteq S$, $K\subseteq B$ and $IS\subseteq S$ are finitely generated. These assertions use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] and the definition [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tag 0ALR, first paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 00FN, 0316 and 05GG

proof.text: The conormal hypothesis says $I^cJ\subseteq J^2$. For any $f\in IS$, also $f^cJ\subseteq J^2$: the extended ideal satisfies $(IS)^c=I^cS$. Thus $J_f=J_f^2$ in $S_f$, since $x/f^n=(f^cx)/f^{n+c}$ for $x\in J$; the reverse inclusion follows because $J_f$ is an ideal. The finitely many generators of $J$ still generate $J_f$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fg-idempotent-ideal-idempotent-generator] to get $J_f=(a_f)$ with $a_f^2=a_f$, and then to the localized surjection $S_f\to C_f$, whose kernel is $J_f$, to identify $C_f=(S_f)_{1-a_f}$. The kernel assertion follows directly from fractions: an element maps to zero precisely when multiplying its numerator by some power of $f$ lands in $J$. This also covers $c=0$.

source.place: Tag 0ALR, first paragraph, applying algebra.tex Tag 00EH

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-punctured-idempotent-complement] to $S\to C$ and the finitely generated ideal $IS$. It gives a quotient $S\twoheadrightarrow C^{\prime}$ for which $\delta_f:S_f\xrightarrow{\sim}T_f$, $s\mapsto(s|_C,s|_{C^{\prime}})$, is an isomorphism for every $f\in IS$, where $T=C\times C^{\prime}$. The $S$-module $T$ is generated by $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ because both factors are quotients. Choose generators $f_1,\ldots,f_t$ of $K\subseteq B$. The map $B\to S$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], and $B/K\to S/KS$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal].

source.place: Tag 0ALR, first paragraph and start of second paragraph; Tag 0C2A

proof.text: Use the algebra datum with completed piece $T$, chart $B_{f_i}$, structural map $\alpha_i=\delta_{f_i}^{-1}:T_{f_i}\to S_{f_i}=B_{f_i}\otimes_B S$, and the canonical chart swaps $\alpha_{ij}$. The two compatibility conditions in [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] hold: on a double localization both structural maps are the inverse of the same map $S_{f_if_j}\to T_{f_if_j}$, and the swaps send $b/(f_i^af_j^b)$ to that same fraction with the denominators reordered. Reordering three denominators gives the cocycle identity. Each chart is generated by $1$ as a module, and $T$ is finite as just shown. Hence [lem-per-formal-glueing-finite-algebras] gives a finite $B$-algebra $D$ and a compatible $S$-algebra isomorphism $D\otimes_B S\cong T$.

source.place: Tag 0ALR, second paragraph, omitted checks (1)(a) and (1)(b) expanded; Tags 05EL, 05ER and 05EU

proof.text: A finite set of $B$-module generators of $D$ also generates it as a $B$-algebra, so adjoining these to finite $A$-algebra generators of $B$ makes $D$ finite type over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. The map $D\to T$ induces an isomorphism $D/ID\cong T/IT$: explicitly, reduce $D\otimes_B S$ modulo $I$ and use $S/IS\cong B/IB$; the maps send $d\otimes\bar b$ to $bd$ and $d$ to $d\otimes1$. Let $\bar e\in D/ID$ correspond to $(1,0)\in C/IC\times C^{\prime}/IC^{\prime}$. The finite-algebra integrality theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes $D$ integral over $B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotent-upstairs], with base ring $B$, ideal $IB$ and integral algebra $D$. It gives an etale map $B\to B^{\prime}$, an isomorphism $B/IB\cong B^{\prime}/IB^{\prime}$, and an idempotent $e\in D^{\prime}=D\otimes_B B^{\prime}$ lifting $\bar e$ under that isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0ALR, second paragraph, construction of the idempotent; Tag 07M4

proof.text: The etaleness just obtained means that $\operatorname{Spec}B^{\prime}\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale in [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence flat. Its affine ring map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], and it is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]. In particular $B^{\prime}$ is a finite-type $B$-algebra, hence finite type over $A$ by concatenating its generators with those of $B$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. The $B^{\prime}$-module $D^{\prime}$ is finite, generated by the images of the chosen $B$-module generators of $D$.

source.place: Tag 0ALR, etale replacement; morphisms.tex Tags 01U5 and 02GJ

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers], the canonical maps $B/I^nB\to B^{\prime}/I^nB^{\prime}$ are isomorphisms for all $n\ge1$. They commute with the quotient maps because all come from $B\to B^{\prime}$. Applying their inverses coordinatewise therefore identifies $S^{\prime}=(B^{\prime})^\wedge$ with $S=B^\wedge$ as $B$-algebras. Let $\beta:B^{\prime}\to S$ be the completion map followed by this identification. For finite $D^{\prime}$, [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] identifies its completion with $S^{\prime}\otimes_{B^{\prime}}D^{\prime}$. This is a ring isomorphism, since its formula $s\otimes d\mapsto s\,\iota(d)$ preserves products on pure tensors and hence on their finite sums. The explicit mutually inverse tensor maps $s\otimes(d\otimes b^{\prime})\mapsto d\otimes s\beta(b^{\prime})$ and $d\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes(d\otimes1)$ now give $(D^{\prime})^\wedge\cong D\otimes_B S\cong T$. All maps are $A$-algebra maps, and their reductions modulo $I$ give the original identification $D/ID\cong T/IT$.

source.place: Tag 0ALR, parenthetical assertion that the completions are unaltered, expanded using the flat-power comparison from Tag 0AGU and algebra.tex Tag 00MA

proof.text: The finite $S$-module $T$ is $I$-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian], since $S$ is Noetherian and complete. Thus $(T,IT)$ is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian]. The image $\epsilon$ of $e$ in $T$ under the completion isomorphism is idempotent and reduces to $(1,0)$ modulo $IT$, by the lifting property and the reduction compatibility in the preceding step. The definition [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], applied to the finite $T$-algebra $T$ itself, says that an idempotent of $T/IT$ has at most one idempotent lift in $T$. Consequently $\epsilon=(1,0)$ in $C\times C^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 0ALR, complete henselian pair and final factor identification; Tag 0ALJ

proof.text: Put $F=D^{\prime}/(1-e)$ and $G=D^{\prime}/(e)$. The map $D^{\prime}\to F\times G$ is an isomorphism: an inverse sends $([x],[y])$ to $ex+(1-e)y$; this is well defined because $e(1-e)=0$, and the two composites are identities using $e+(1-e)=1$. Both $F$ and $G$ are finite-type $A$-algebras, since quotients preserve a finite set of algebra generators and $D^{\prime}$ is finite over the finite-type $A$-algebra $B^{\prime}$. Modulo every $I^n$ this product decomposition is $D^{\prime}/I^nD^{\prime}=F/I^nF\times G/I^nG$. Taking compatible sequences coordinatewise yields $(D^{\prime})^\wedge\cong F^\wedge\times G^\wedge$, with $e$ selecting the first factor. Under the previous isomorphism with $T=C\times C^{\prime}$, the same idempotent is $(1,0)$. Restricting to its image therefore gives $F^\wedge\cong C$ as $A$-algebras, as required.

source.place: Tag 0ALR, final sentence: split the lifted idempotent and complete the two factors
